claims.text: The FeNiCrCoCu coating has an FCC structure at 300 K.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating has a high dislocation density at 300 K.
The proposed intervention is nanoindentation to 30 Å at 10 m/s at 900 K and 1200 K.
A vacuum or inert atmosphere prevents oxide formation and thereby isolates mechanical effects.
Above 900 K, the FeNiCrCoCu/Cu system undergoes a thermally activated transition from dislocation-mediated plasticity to mechanical amorphization.
The stacking-fault energy of the FeNiCrCoCu coating collapses above 900 K.
Temperature can substantially affect stacking-fault energy and FCC-HCP stability in transition-metal HEAs.
High configurational entropy and atomic-size mismatch produce lattice distortion in the HEA coating.
The proposed SFE collapse promotes nucleation of partial dislocations.
The nucleated partial dislocations rapidly annihilate or fail to propagate, causing dislocation starvation.
High-rate indentation combined with thermal disorder causes a localized FCC-to-amorphous transformation.
The high-temperature transformation produces an amorphous state rather than stable HCP twins or precipitates.
The resulting amorphous layer has low shear strength.
The resulting amorphous layer has high adhesion to the Cu matrix.
The amorphous layer causes a sharp increase in friction coefficient and rapid material removal.
Above 900 K, total dislocation line length will decrease.
HCP atom count will transiently increase and then rapidly decrease as amorphization develops.
The elastic modulus will decrease nonlinearly in correlation with amorphous-layer onset.
Simple thermal softening would produce a linear decrease in hardness through increased dislocation mobility without a sudden friction spike.
In polycrystalline HEAs, grain-boundary sliding may dominate over the proposed single-crystal mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires thermally activated disordering and amorphization, but the falsification rule says persistence of the friction spike when thermal disordering is suppressed would support the hypothesis. Such persistence would instead undermine the stated disorder-driven mechanism.
